function: Excluded (no_learning): ReDBeam is a GPU-parallel randomized search with zero-forcing sampling and scaling local search for MU-MIMO beamforming; no trained model (p. 2, p. 6, p. 7).
notes: Excluded for no_learning (code 3); codes 1 and 2 do not apply (research article proposing a method). ReDBeam is a parallel optimization heuristic for MU-MIMO beamforming, not a trained model: it builds zero-forcing basis vectors from N noisy CSI samples (p. 6), draws random initial solutions, p. 7: "we generate L initial solutions within this cone via random sampling", and refines them with a scaling local search (p. 7, p. 8), all run on a GPU (p. 9, p. 10). There is no neural network, training set or learned parameter. p. 2: "does not need a complicated offline training process", and p. 6: "ReDBeam is a parallel algorithm that is suitable for implementation on GPU". The benchmarks are D2BF (convex approximation and SDP), Gaussian Approximation and Mean Approximation, all non-learned (p. 13). 'Data-driven' here means working directly on CSI samples through a Wasserstein ambiguity set (p. 5), not machine learning.
